newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel approves free trade with Czech, Slovakia.
newsitem.headline: Israel approves free trade with Czech, Slovakia.

text.p: The Israeli government has approved free trade agreements reached with Slovakia and the Czech Republic, the Industry and Trade Ministry said on Sunday.
The agreements, which go into effect on January 1, 1997, will allow Israel to compete with European countries whose goods are exempt from tariffs in the two central European states.
Slovakia and the Czech Republic are associate members of the European Union, giving them favoured trade status with European countries.
Israeli trade with the two states is valued at around $100 million a year, the ministry said.
The statement said the agreement covers trade in industrial, agricultural and food products.
